scope: Complete per-glyph Korean dictionary order, direction, boundary and form crosscheck. Not exam-body certification.

entries.notes: 言 seven and the upper 免 of 毚 (8-16) sit in the same order, but at position 18 the dictionary draws a shallow stroke descending to the right across the lower block where the licensed MM original draws a short rightward head turning into a downward sweep, and the finished 毚 blocks differ there. Order and direction cannot bridge the stroke-shape difference, so the glyph is held

疒 five matches, but the dictionary writes the four side strokes of the 脊 top as horizontal bars, two on the left and two on the right, where the licensed MM original draws four short slanted marks around the 人. Order and direction cannot bridge the form difference, so the glyph is held, as 朕 was for the interior of 月

The dictionary opens with the long 丿 and 乀 and then writes four horizontal bars, two on the left and two on the right, where the licensed MM original writes four short slanted marks first and the two long sweeps afterwards. The bars and the slanted marks are different forms, which order and direction cannot bridge, so the glyph is held. 月 (7-10) agrees

The short vertical and bar open the same way (1-2), but the two pen lifts differ from there: the dictionary joins the left vertical with the bottom bar into one stroke and finishes with the right vertical, where the licensed MM original writes the left vertical alone, joins the top hump with the right vertical, and finishes with the bottom bar. The stroke boundaries, not just their order, differ, so the glyph is held
